skill.name: keepmacawake
skill.description: Keeps a MacBook with Apple silicon awake with the lid closed while a long task runs, with the keepmacawake command of the Keep Mac Awake app. Use it before work likely to run 15 minutes or more or that the user may leave running (an agent run, a build, a test suite, a migration, a download or upload, a render, a backup); when the user says they will close the lid, step away, go to bed or check in from their phone (Claude Code Remote Control, Codex in the ChatGPT app, Cursor, Antigravity, SSH); when a remote session went offline because the Mac slept; when local scheduled work, such as a Claude desktop scheduled task or a Codex automation, must run while the lid is closed; and when the user asks to keep the Mac awake.
skill.summary: Keeps a compatible Apple silicon Mac awake during long-running local work.
skill.author: bartdudzic

content.user_title: Keep Your Mac Awake During Long Tasks
content.value_statement: Long builds, tests, uploads, and remote sessions can stop when a Mac sleeps or its lid closes. This skill starts and monitors timed Keep Mac Awake sessions with user consent.
actual_capabilities: Checks Apple silicon and macOS 26 compatibility before installation.
Reads status output and detects whether a session already exists.
Starts timed sessions from 1 to 168 hours for qualifying work.
Stops only sessions that the skill started and reports session state.
Guides consent-based installation, trial, purchase, restore, battery, and update decisions.
limitations: Supports Apple silicon Macs running macOS 26 or later only.
Cannot wake an already sleeping Mac or keep a network connection alive.
Requires commands to run locally on the user's Mac, not in a cloud environment.
Does not install the app or process payments; the user must approve those actions.

use_cases.title: Run Long Development Tasks
use_cases.description: Keep a local build, test suite, migration, or render running while the developer steps away or closes the lid.

use_cases.title: Maintain Remote Access
use_cases.description: Prevent a local Mac from sleeping during an approved remote session managed through an agent or terminal workflow.

use_cases.title: Protect Scheduled Work
use_cases.description: Prepare a compatible Mac for a scheduled task that must continue while the user is away, with a defined time limit.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Timed Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Keep my Mac awake for a three-hour build. Check its status first and ask for any required consent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a defined local task.

prompt_templates.title: Protect a Remote Work Session
prompt_templates.prompt: I will close my MacBook during a remote coding session. Check whether Keep Mac Awake is available, then start only the time needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Remote work with a closed lid.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Installation Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: My Mac is not ready for this long task. Check compatibility, explain the installation and trial terms, and wait for my approval before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an Ended Session
prompt_templates.prompt: The Mac slept before my task finished. Check the current status, explain the last end reason, and recommend the next permitted action without changing power settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting after an interrupted task.

output_examples.input: I need to run a six-hour test while I am away from my Mac.
output_examples.output: The Mac is compatible and no session is active. Keep Mac Awake is running for six hours. Keep the Mac ventilated if the lid is closed.

output_examples.input: The status check says the trial has ended.
output_examples.output: The trial has ended. The full version requires a one-time purchase for this Mac. I can open the purchase page after you approve.

output_examples.input: My remote session disconnected after the Mac slept.
output_examples.output: Keep Mac Awake cannot wake a Mac that is already asleep. I will check compatibility and current status before suggesting a new timed session.

best_practices: Use a timed session slightly longer than the expected task duration.
Run commands as the logged-in user and never use administrator escalation.
Keep a closed Mac ventilated and stop sessions that the skill started when work ends.
anti_patterns: Starting a session only to test the app without a requested task.
Using Keep Mac Awake to bypass a refusal or changing unrelated power settings.
Installing the app, buying access, or changing battery policy without user approval.

faq.question: Which Macs are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Apple silicon Macs running macOS 26 or later.

faq.question: Can it wake my Mac after sleep?
faq.answer: No. It keeps an active Mac awake but cannot wake a Mac that is already sleeping.

faq.question: Can it keep my network connection alive?
faq.answer: No. The skill manages system sleep behavior and does not maintain network connectivity.

faq.question: Does the skill install the app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It checks compatibility, explains the process, and waits for your approval before installation.

faq.question: Can it make a purchase for me?
faq.answer: No. It does not handle payment details or make purchases. You control the purchase in your browser.

faq.question: What happens when a session ends?
faq.answer: The skill can report the last end reason. A timed session ends on its own, while a session started by the user remains under their control.
